slot.brief: Block on incline with applied force shown in diagram; find range of force for equilibrium given friction coefficient

stem:
A block of mass $4\ \text{kg}$ rests on a rough inclined plane of inclination $37^\circ$. An external force $F$ is applied parallel to the incline, directed up the slope, as shown in the figure. If the coefficient of static friction between the block and the incline is $\mu_s = 0.25$, the range of $F$ for which the block remains in equilibrium is:
(Take $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$, $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$)

verdicts.working: Gravity component along incline: mg sin37° = 4·10·0.6 = 24 N. Normal force N = mg cos37° = 32 N, so max static friction f = 0.25·32 = 8 N. Equilibrium requires |F − 24| ≤ 8, giving 16 N ≤ F ≤ 32 N.

working:
1. Normal force acting on the block:
$$N = mg\cos 37^\circ = 4 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 32\ \text{N}$$

2. Maximum static friction force:
$$f_s^{\max} = \mu_s N = 0.25 \times 32 = 8\ \text{N}$$

3. Component of gravity directed down the incline:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin 37^\circ = 4 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 24\ \text{N}$$

4. For equilibrium, two limiting cases exist:
- Lower limit ($F_{\min}$): The block tends to slide down, so static friction acts upwards along the incline:
$$F_{\min} + f_s^{\max} = mg\sin 37^\circ \implies F_{\min} = 24 - 8 = 16\ \text{N}$$

- Upper limit ($F_{\max}$): The block tends to slide up, so static friction acts downwards along the incline:
$$F_{\max} = mg\sin 37^\circ + f_s^{\max} \implies F_{\max} = 24 + 8 = 32\ \text{N}$$

Thus, the range of force for equilibrium is:
$$16\ \text{N} \le F \le 32\ \text{N}$$

Independent check: Gravity component along incline: mg sin37° = 4·10·0.6 = 24 N. Normal force N = mg cos37° = 32 N, so max static friction f = 0.25·32 = 8 N. Equilibrium requires |F − 24| ≤ 8, giving 16 N ≤ F ≤ 32 N.

figure.description: A right-angled triangular wedge rests on a horizontal surface. The hypotenuse forms an inclined plane rising from left to right at an angle of 37 degrees to the horizontal. A rectangular block labeled with mass 4 kg is positioned on the inclined face. An arrow labeled 'F' originates from the block and points upwards along and parallel to the inclined surface.
